candidates.change_summary: Remove the balance transfer to owner, so contract retains ether after go() instead of forwarding it to owner.
Change target address so the call is sent to a different recipient, potentially altering subsequent balance available for owner transfer.
Make the target.call value zero instead of msg.value, so sent ether stays in contract and increases the amount transferred to owner.
Remove the require statement so execution continues even if the target call fails, altering contract balance and owner transfer outcome.
Transfer a fixed amount instead of full contract balance to owner, changing `go` behavior and final state.
Replace `target` with the `owner` address as the call recipient, sending the contract's value to the owner before the final transfer.
Replace `target.call` with `target.delegatecall`, preserving value behavior incorrectly and changing observable execution semantics.
Replace `target.call` with `target.staticcall`, preventing value transfer to the target and changing observable state.
Replace the call value `msg.value` with the contract's full balance, changing the amount sent to the target.
Replace the final transfer recipient `owner` with `target`, changing the observable balance distribution.
Replace the final transfer amount with `msg.value`, changing the amount sent to the owner.
Delete the `require(__sent_result100);` statement, allowing execution to continue even when the target call fails.
Delete the final owner transfer, leaving the contract balance unwithdrawn after a successful target call.
Delete the target call, causing `go` to skip payment to the target and only transfer the contract balance to the owner.
Move the final owner transfer before the target call, changing observable balances and call ordering.
Replace the call value from msg.value to zero, so the external target receives no ETH while the function still sends the contract balance to owner.
Require the call result to be false instead of true, so the function can only proceed when the external call fails.
Delete the require on the external call result, allowing the function to continue regardless of whether the target call succeeds.
Transfer the entire contract balance to the target address instead of to owner after the external call.
Transfer a fixed amount of 0 to owner instead of the whole contract balance.
Delete the final transfer to owner, so the contract balance is not sent out at the end of go.
Call the external target with empty calldata using a high-level call with zero value instead of forwarding msg.value.
Send the contract balance to owner before making the external target call instead of after it.
Send the full contract balance to owner via a low-level call instead of transfer, removing the 2300 gas stipend and revert-on-failure semantics.
Change the external target address to the zero address while keeping the same call and balance transfer behavior.
Change the external target address to the owner address, altering which contract receives the forwarded ETH and call.
Make the function non-payable so calls sending nonzero value revert, changing go's externally visible payoff behavior.
Replace the target address constant with a different address, changing where the external call sends ETH.
Remove the require on the external call success, so a failed target call no longer reverts go().
Remove the transfer of the contract balance to owner, leaving the forwarded value at the target without sweeping remaining balance.
Change the recipient of the final balance transfer from owner to msg.sender.
Replace the transfer of the entire contract balance to owner with no transfer, leaving the balance in the contract.
Transfer only a fixed zero value to owner instead of the contract balance.
Send msg.value back to owner instead of the current contract balance.
Remove the require on the external call result so a failing call no longer reverts.
Invert the require condition so go reverts when the external call succeeds and proceeds when it fails.
Send the entire contract balance to the fixed target address instead of owner.
Transfer only msg.value to owner instead of the remaining contract balance.
Replace the fallback call target address with the zero address so the external call behavior changes.
Change the low-level call value from msg.value to 0, preventing value from being forwarded.
Change the post-call transfer recipient from owner to the target address.
Change the post-call transfer amount from the contract balance to zero.
Remove the require on the low-level call success flag, allowing execution to continue even if the call fails.
Delete the post-call transfer to owner, leaving the contract balance unchanged after a successful go call.
Move the transfer to owner before the external call, changing the balance available for the call and reverting behavior on call failure.
Replace the owner transfer recipient with the calling account (msg.sender).
Replace the owner transfer recipient with the contract itself.
Transfer only half of the contract balance to the owner.
Skip the owner balance transfer entirely.
Ignore the external call result and proceed without requiring success.
Send zero value instead of msg.value to the external target.
Move the owner balance transfer before the external call and require.
Change owner state variable reference to msg.sender in the final transfer
Replace the require on the external call result with a require(true), so failed external calls no longer revert the transaction.
Replace the transfer of the full contract balance to owner with a transfer of zero, leaving the balance in the contract.
Replace the owner address in the final transfer with the zero address.
Replace the call value with zero, so the contract no longer forwards msg.value to target.
Replace the target address constant with a different non-contract address, changing where the forwarded value is sent.
Remove the require on the external call result so a failing call still completes and transfers the balance.
Delete the transfer line so the owner receives no funds after the external call.
Replace the recipient of the final transfer with the caller so the owner does not receive the balance.
Replace the recipient of the final transfer with the contract itself; transfer to self reverts.
Make the require check the negation of the external call result, so success and failure flip.
Replace the require(__sent_result100) with require(true), making go complete even when the external call fails.
Delete the require(__sent_result100), making go complete even when the external call fails.
Delete the require(__sent_result100) check after the external call, allowing go() to complete even when the target call fails.
Delete the final transfer of the contract balance to owner, so go() completes without paying out any balance.
Replace the outgoing call target address with the zero address, causing the call to behave differently (likely success with no code) instead of reverting on the original target.
Delete the require(__sent_result100) check after the low-level call, so the function no longer reverts when the target call fails.
Delete the final owner transfer so the function completes without attempting to send the contract balance to the owner.
Replace the low-level target.call value with zero, so the target call receives no ether and may succeed where it previously failed.
Replace the low-level target.call with a transfer to the target address, which reverts when the target rejects or cannot receive the ether.
Delete the low-level target.call entirely, so the function no longer depends on whether the target call succeeds.
Replace the target address with the zero address, changing whether the low-level call can succeed.
Replace the final owner transfer recipient with the target address, changing whether the balance transfer succeeds and where funds go.
Removed the require that the external call to target succeeded, so a call that fails in P can complete in the mutant.
Removed the transfer of the contract balance to owner, so a call that succeeds in P acts differently in the mutant.
Replaced the hardcoded target address with the zero address, changing the call behavior on go().
Changed the value sent with the external call from msg.value to zero, altering the call's outcome on go().
Changed the owner transfer recipient to msg.sender, so funds go to the caller instead of owner.
Replace the forwarded call value with zero so the required external call no longer needs matching ETH, changing whether go() reverts.
Remove the payment to owner after the external call, leaving the contract balance unchanged instead of transferring it.
Change the outgoing call amount from msg.value to 0, so the transfer to owner occurs without first requiring a successful value transfer.
Change the target address from the hardcoded address to the zero address, so the external call behaves differently.
Change the hardcoded target address to address(this), so the external call invokes the contract's own fallback instead of the original target.
Replace the outgoing call with a plain value transfer to the target, changing the call semantics and gas/fallback behavior.
Delete the require statement checking the success of the outgoing call, so a failed call no longer reverts and the owner transfer still executes.
Negate the require condition so the function reverts when the outgoing call succeeds and continues when it fails.
Replace the outgoing call with a staticcall, which rejects value and prevents state changes, changing success/revert behavior.
Replace the owner transfer with a transfer to the caller, changing who receives the contract balance and thus the observable balance behavior.
Delete the owner balance transfer, so the contract retains its balance after a successful outgoing call.
Move the owner balance transfer before the outgoing call, so the contract sends its balance to the owner before forwarding msg.value.
Replace the require of the sent result with require that the call failed, so a successful external call makes go revert.
Delete the require on the external call result, so go completes even when the target call fails.
Change the value sent in the external call from msg.value to 0, so it fails differently and go reverts when msg.value is nonzero.
Change the recipient of the final balance transfer from owner to this contract, so the transfer does not forward the balance to owner.
Change the final transfer amount from the contract balance to 0, so no balance is forwarded to owner.
Change the call target address to the zero address, so the external call fails and go reverts.
Change the call target address to the owner address, so the external call goes to a different target and may fail.
